scope: Engine-light XR UI shell: panel, wrist-menu, and hand-menu identity, a shell layout model (anchor kinds world, head-locked, wrist, hand; placement intents open, close, focus, dock, follow) applied to an immutable shell state with stable failure codes and deterministic replay, pointer and gaze routing as typed intents that resolve to exactly one panel, and a skin contract mapping the shared design-language tokens to a closed set of named slots, with sibling UGUI and UI Toolkit adapters planned separately, each carrying one injectable skin seam and a default skin
review_note: The URLs below were not fetched from the authoring environment because its network egress policy blocks them; the admitted claims come from the author's prior reading of these documents and must be confirmed by a person, together with the exact page paths and version pins, before the admission record is signed.

sources.maintenance_evidence: Unity UI (UGUI) 2.0 is the version pinned by this repository's compatibility profiles and its Canvas manual is maintained with the package; page path and version pin to be confirmed by a person; not fetched from this environment
sources.admitted_role: UGUI adapter boundary: a world-space Canvas is the renderer surface that one shell panel binds to, and its placement is a transform owned outside the Canvas
admitted_claims: A Canvas has a render mode, and World Space places the Canvas as a rectangle in the scene whose position, rotation, and scale come from its transform rather than from the screen
A world-space Canvas needs an event camera reference for UI raycasting, and a missing event camera is a configuration fault rather than a rendering choice
Every UI element must be a child of a Canvas, so one panel maps to one Canvas subtree rather than to loose elements
excluded_uses: Core does not reference Canvas, RectTransform, Graphic, EventSystem, or any other engine or UI type
No claim that a world-space Canvas is legible, reachable, or comfortable at any distance or on any device without a Device Lab receipt

sources.admitted_role: UGUI adapter routing boundary: the toolkit's XR UI input module and tracked-device graphic raycaster are the components that turn an interactor into UGUI pointer events for a world-space Canvas
admitted_claims: UGUI interaction in XR requires one EventSystem with an XR UI input module in place of the standalone input module, and a tracked-device graphic raycaster on each world-space Canvas
Ray and poke interactors implement a UI interactor contract and the input module polls them to produce hover, press, and scroll pointer events
A Canvas without the tracked-device raycaster, or a scene without the XR UI input module, receives no XR pointer events and reports nothing
excluded_uses: Core does not reference XRUIInputModule, TrackedDeviceGraphicRaycaster, IUIInteractor, or any other toolkit type

sources.admitted_role: Routing boundary for gaze as a named input source: gaze hovers and assists, and selection from gaze is an explicit, opt-in configuration rather than the default pointer
admitted_claims: A gaze interactor is a ray interactor driven by eye or head pose whose hover is separate from selection, and interactables opt in to gaze interaction rather than receiving it by default
Gaze assistance can snap or enlarge targeting for another interactor, so gaze and a controller or hand ray are distinct named sources that can act on the same target

context_only_not_derivation_inputs.reason: The shared design language defines the tokens, state model, and renderer adapter contract that this family's skin contract maps to a closed slot set; it is the visual and interaction reference the shell adopts, not a derivation input for the shell's layout or routing model

The Inventory presentation adapters become one client of the shell through the renderer-named XR compositions; Inventory code, samples, and evidence are neither derivation inputs nor transferable evidence for this family

The Interaction family routes semantic intents to handlers; the shell resolves which panel a pointer or gaze event targets. The two must not duplicate each other, and a panel-as-context seam is a later proposal

source_gate_non_claims: No source grants package maturity, release, certification, platform review outcome, or device authority

The first implementation is a panel-identity, layout-state, routing, and skin-contract substrate, not a window manager, a raycaster, an input reader, a hand-tracking consumer, or a rendering component

Legibility, comfort, reach, hand-tracking behaviour, and any headset, controller, or eye-tracking behaviour are device claims that require a Device Lab receipt, never an EditMode result or a source citation
Automated or device evidence recorded for the UGUI adapter never transfers to the UI Toolkit adapter or the reverse
